facts: Sky emerged from the long-running MakerDAO project during its 2024 rebranding.
Rune Christensen was among Maker's most visible founders and governance voices.
Maker had become famous for creating the DAI decentralized stablecoin.
The new Sky identity introduced changes involving the governance asset and USDS stablecoin.
SKY is tied to governance and ecosystem incentives rather than a simple dollar redemption promise.
The proposed migration from MKR created important choices for existing community participants.
Token-based voting became a central theme in how the system allocated risk and resources.
Debates about centralization, collateral choices, and compliance persisted through the transition.
DeFi communities compared the new branding with Maker's earlier decentralization ideals.
The role of USDS differs from that of SKY despite their shared ecosystem.
Governance value can fluctuate sharply even when an associated stablecoin targets one dollar.
Contract upgrades and migration programs require careful security and communication.
Some supporters saw a chance to broaden the ecosystem's audience and products.
The story of Sky shows that blockchain governance can involve difficult organizational redesign.
bridge: SKY is a governance asset connected to a stablecoin ecosystem, whereas PROI points do not currently vote on a chain.

facts: Pump.fun emerged on Solana during 2024 as a platform associated with meme-token creation.
Alon Cohen, Dylan Kerler, and Noah Tweedale have been identified in reporting as its founders.
The platform became prominent during a wave of unusually rapid meme-asset launches.
Easy token creation drew both curious communities and concerns about financial speculation.
Public data showed large bursts of activity during several market cycles.
Critics emphasized scams, manipulation, and the difficulty of evaluating newly created tokens.
Supporters described a new style of online community experimentation.
The project introduced its own PUMP token in July 2025.
A token associated with an application does not prove that its underlying content is safe.
High public interest made the platform controversial far beyond technical cryptocurrency circles.
Legal and moderation debates formed part of its ongoing history.
Launchpad fees and incentive structures can create conflicts between operators and participants.
Many meme assets do not survive after their initial attention fades.
Pump.fun's story is better understood as a lesson in viral market behavior than as a recommendation to participate.
bridge: PUMP's link to rapid speculative token launches is a reason to distinguish PROI's non-financial rewards from trading incentives.

facts: OpenUSD is a comparatively new dollar-token project connected to Open Standard.
The OUSD rollout occurred during 2026 as the market for institutional stablecoins broadened.
Open Standard emphasized sharing portions of reserve economics with distribution partners.
Zach Abrams was named publicly as a senior executive associated with the stablecoin initiative.
Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe, and Visa were identified among founding partners.
The project promoted interoperability across multiple blockchain infrastructures.
OUSD is designed to track the dollar rather than increase because of engineered scarcity.
Digital-dollar products require reserve, custody, and redemption arrangements.
Revenue-sharing models raise questions about governance and partner incentives.
The participation of major brands should not be misconstrued as a promise of risk-free ownership.
OpenUSD's brief operating history cannot yet support sweeping claims about resilience across decades.
The token became visible in a crowded field containing USDC, USDT, and other dollar instruments.
Regulatory differences between jurisdictions may affect distribution and usage.
OUSD illustrates how payment networks and blockchain settlement are becoming increasingly connected.
bridge: OUSD is a recently issued dollar stablecoin, while PROI has no issuer-backed dollar claim and remains only points.

facts: Morpho grew from efforts to make decentralized lending markets more efficient.
Paul Frambot became one of the project's recognizable founders.
Early designs focused on improving lending-rate matching around established DeFi infrastructure.
The protocol later evolved toward more modular lending markets.
Morpho Blue introduced a distinct design for creating narrowly configured credit markets.
Market curators and collateral rules became important elements of the surrounding ecosystem.
The MORPHO token is connected with project governance.
Protocol development attracted attention from investors and DeFi engineering teams.
Lower overhead does not eliminate liquidation, oracle, or smart-contract risk.
Borrowing and lending through software require careful definitions of collateral and insolvency.
Governance decisions can affect markets with very different risk profiles.
Morpho's public narrative often emphasizes permissionless infrastructure rather than a conventional bank.
Market valuations responded to the growth and competition of decentralized finance.
Morpho offers a clear example of financial infrastructure that cannot be reduced to one token price.
bridge: Morpho manages lending-market governance, whereas PROI points are not collateral and do not authorize borrowing.

facts: Ethereum Classic emerged from the bitter disagreement surrounding Ethereum's 2016 DAO exploit.
Some participants rejected rewriting blockchain history to reverse effects of the incident.
The chain that retained the earlier rule set became known as Ethereum Classic.
ETC and ETH therefore share an origin but have separate modern networks.
The event became a foundational debate over immutability and community governance.
Supporters argued that blockchain history should remain unchanged even after painful events.
Critics argued that exceptional interventions could protect users in unprecedented circumstances.
Ethereum Classic continued as a proof-of-work system while Ethereum later adopted proof of stake.
Barry Silbert and other public figures have been associated with historical support for ETC.
Like other proof-of-work networks, ETC has faced questions about the security of mining power.
Several reported chain-reorganization incidents intensified those concerns.
Application ecosystems and developer resources diverged sharply between the two Ethereum networks.
ETC has experienced major market cycles without simply following every Ethereum upgrade.
Its story demonstrates that technical protocols are also shaped by human choices about governance.
bridge: Ethereum Classic is a real alternative chain formed by a historical fork, unlike PROI points, which have never launched a chain.
